Adjusted interpretation with Beige Book: The March 20 FOMC statement highlights solid growth, strong job gains, easing but still-elevated inflation, and a continued hold at 5.25–5.50% with ongoing QT. Beige Book reports since January indicate only modest increases in activity across Districts, steady-to-slightly-firmer consumer spending on retail goods, greater labor availability with easing wage pressures, and some businesses (e.g., restaurants) absorbing price pressures—signs of moderating inflation and narrower margins rather than broad demand acceleration. At the same time, office CRE remains a notable stress point (including in New York), aligning with tighter credit conditions and softer loan demand seen in SLOOS. Together, these point to a resilient but not re-accelerating economy, with balanced-but-cautious risks and headwinds from credit and CRE that temper the FOMC’s otherwise constructive tone.

Net effect: modestly positive macro backdrop, but Beige Book- and SLOOS-consistent headwinds reduce the overall positivity of the statement.
